rear rails · battery: Big Boi, UDM, switch, PDU Pro
ZWA-2 is too big for a shelf: top of the rack or
wall-mounted beside it. Both sticks hang off Big Boi
(U15–U20) on USB 2.0 extensions: Zigbee down to the
hub shelf, ZWA-2 up to the top. Re-map both in the HA VM.
Panel A feeds the Enterprise 48's top row, panel B its
bottom row: every cord 6". The UDM only routes: WAN in,
one 10G DAC up to the switch. All clients and rack gear
sit on the switch. 400 mm deep on 18" (457 mm) rails:
the power cord sits just past the rear rail.
Hue, Lutron, HDHomeRun, Ting ONT and the Zigbee
dongle under the UDM, with about 80 mm (3.1") clear.
Their cables run up the rear into panel B. The
CenturyLink ONT stays outside in its box.
One brush plate, over the PDU Pro
The PDU outlets face front: cords from the gear above
run down the rear, come forward through the brush
and drop into the outlets. Ordered, in the rack on day one,
fed from the 4th UPS battery outlet: everything on it is
on battery (hub shelf, second server, Sonos Amp).
Brush plate at U21 gives airflow and a cable path.
If the 12S4 is 272 mm, not 262, it hits that plate:
measure before mounting. Support it from below.
10G DAC up the rear, through panel B (B20), to the switch.
About 130 mm clear: Sonos Amp (64 mm) now, room for
a Mac Studio (95 mm) later. Side by side is tight.
Shelf, headroom and U11 sit between it and Big Boi;
U11 keeps the 3U-case option open. On the PDU Pro,
434 W × 341 D mm, 167 mm tall with feet; fold the
antennas back and shelf + receiver fit 4U. U8 stays
open for lid vents. 460 W rated: a UPS surge-only
outlet, not the PDU. Wire HEOS by Ethernet.
UPS at the very bottom, U3 open
Battery outlets: Big Boi, UDM, Enterprise 48, PDU Pro.
Surge-only: receiver. With the switch, PoE gear and the
PDU's load, roughly 350–400 W: about 15 min of runtime
PDU Pro 8.2 · 2 CLV shelves 11.0 · 2 brush plates 1.9

2026-11-15 draft v12 · both are UniFi 24-port keystone panels · fill = patch cord colour · dashed = run not pulled or gear not bought
Patch panel A (U30) → Enterprise 48 top row: security, endpoints, sensors
Security A1–A8, endpoints A9–A16, presence sensors A17–A19, A20–A21 free; server links A22–A24 over the switch's SFP+ cages
Patch panel B (U28) → Enterprise 48 bottom row: rack gear and networking
Rack gear B1–B6 (from the rear), B7–B12 free, UniFi networking B13–B24: UPS and PDU, APs, switches, WAN down to the UDM
Switch = USW Enterprise 48 PoE (on the UPS): 48× 2.5 GbE PoE+ (32 W per port, 720 W), 4× SFP+. Panel A position n sits over column n (top row),
panel B position n under column n (bottom row). Port numbers assume odd on top, even below (UniFi convention; confirm on the switch).
Switch ports behind A22–A24 and B23–B24 stay free: A22–A24 carry server links to the SFP+ cages, B23–B24 patch down to the UDM. Rack gear enters panel B from the back.
Dark = run exists, port reserved, left unpatched until used. Each group keeps a spare at its end; A20–A21 and B7–B12 are free.
